references.notes: The archaeological article reproduces the plan, a labelled plan overlay at the Court Gate and a reconstruction of the east precinct around 1670. The painted bird’s-eye view guides the hierarchy of brick ranges, the Privy Garden frontage, the stone Banqueting House and the high-roofed hall and chapel.
Fisher’s 1680 ground plan as published by Vertue documents the wider palace, including West Whitehall. This draft uses the east precinct visible in the 1670 plan.
The Banqueting House construction dates to 1619–1622. Wyatt’s northern annexe was added in 1809. The plan fit uses the original main hall independently of the later annex.

The higher-resolution Fisher engraving labels the Tennis Court, Cockpit, Tiltyard, Horse Guard Yard, Park Gate and western lodgings. It supplies the traced western court arrangement. Heights and roofing follow the exterior reconstruction’s visual convention.

limitations: Models both sides of Whitehall, including the open Tiltyard and Horse Guard Yard, the Cockpit, Tennis Court, service ranges, and the linked palace and river lodgings. Inaccessible interiors, precise room divisions and unrecorded secondary structures are outside this exterior reconstruction.
The surveyed plans constrain the surviving hall, major courts and the enclosure. The Cockpit roof, lost facades, heights, glazing and roof profiles are interpretive.

The original shoreline is traced along the palace frontage. Present-day elevation samples are retained as controls. Dated alteration of reclaimed land, modern building overlap and the historical water surface remain under review.
